chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from some of our companions, raising it (to the Imam):

Regarding the antelope and the wild donkey that are intercepted with the sword and cut in two — so he said: There is no problem with eating both of them, as long as one of the two halves is not moving. But if one of the two moves, then the other shall not be eaten, because it is carrion.

key_terms.الظَّبْيِ: gazelle/antelope — a permissible game animal in Islamic law
key_terms.النِّصْفَيْنِ: the two halves — the result of the bisection by the sword
key_terms.حِمَارِ الْوَحْشِ: wild donkey (onager) — a permissible game animal, distinct from the domestic donkey which is forbidden
key_terms.مَيْتَةٌ: mayta (carrion) — an animal that died without proper Islamic slaughter, forbidden to eat
key_terms.يُعْتَرَضَانِ: to intercept/hunt — the act of blocking the path of game animals while hunting
key_terms.يُقَدَّانِ: to be cut/split in two — the sword strike that divides the animal

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat a gazelle or wild donkey that is cut in two by a sword while hunting in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a jurisprudential ruling from an Imam (peace be upon him) concerning the permissibility of eating wild game — specifically gazelles and wild donkeys — that are struck and cut in two by a sword while being hunted. The ruling establishes that both halves are permissible to eat provided neither half shows signs of movement after being cut. However, if one half moves after the cut, this indicates that the animal was still alive at the point of division, meaning the cut itself served as the slaughter only for the half that did not move; the moving half is considered to have died subsequently without proper slaughter (dhabiha), rendering it carrion (mayta) and forbidden.
word_analysis: so they are cut in two

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al nazar Bin Suweyd, from one of our companions, raising it,

‘With regards to the antelope and the wild donkey hunted by the sword, so they are both cut, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with eating both of them for as long as one of the two halves is not moving. So if one of the two is moving, the other one would not be eaten as it is dead’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from certain persons of our people in a marfu‘ manner the following is narrated:

“About the case of a deer or wild donkey hunted with sword; if it is cut in pieces, he (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful to use both pieces for food if one of them is not still moving, but if one piece moves, the other piece then is not edible because it is dead.’”
